sentences.sentence: It links pain that is worse with walking, usually in people over 45, with osteoarthritis.

sentences.sentence: NHS 111 Wales describes osteoarthritis as the most common type of arthritis in the UK.

sentences.sentence: Gout is a form of arthritis in which small crystals form inside and around the joints.

sentences.sentence: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune condition in which the immune system attacks the lining of the joints, usually in the hands, feet and wrists, with pain that is typically worse in the mornings or after inactivity.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: The NHS says rheumatoid arthritis is usually first felt in the small joints of the hands and feet.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: The NHS arthritis overview says gout often affects the big toe joint, which can become painful, swollen and hot.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Psoriatic arthritis is a long-term condition that causes joint pain, swelling and stiffness, and the NHS says it affects about 1 in 4 people who have the skin condition psoriasis.

sentences.sentence: The NHS says to rest the joint but not stop moving it altogether, and that a pharmacist or GP can advise about painkillers.

sentences.sentence: Losing weight and eating a balanced diet also help.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: For osteoarthritis the NHS says treatment focuses on exercise, weight management, pain relief and supportive measures such as hot or cold packs.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: NHS 111 Wales says osteoarthritis has no cure but does not necessarily get worse over time.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: The NHS suggests a GP appointment if joint pain stops normal activities or affects sleep, keeps getting worse or coming back, or has not improved after 2 weeks of treating it at home.

sentences.sentence: It also lists joints that stay stiff for more than 30 minutes after waking.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: For gout, the NHS advises seeing a GP for a first episode, or when the usual treatments are not helping.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: The NHS advises an urgent GP appointment or NHS 111 for severe pain and swelling in one joint that started suddenly.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: A warm, swollen joint that is hard to move, with a high temperature or feeling hot and shivery, may mean a joint infection called septic arthritis.

sentences.sentence: A GP examines the joints for swelling, checks how easily they move and asks about symptoms.

sentences.sentence: Blood tests such as ESR, CRP and a full blood count may be used, and X-rays or MRI scans may show inflammation and damage.

sentences.sentence: There is no single definitive test for rheumatoid arthritis, so diagnosis can be difficult.

sentences.sentence: If rheumatoid arthritis is suspected, the GP usually refers the person to a rheumatologist.
